title: The Voicemail — EN/ES/FR (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 100bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal Spanish French life philosophy language learning memory
lyrics:
[Verse 1 — English]
I leave voicemails that begin with "it's me" as if you know
As if you've been waiting specifically for this show
Then I say my name and then I say it again
And then I say "anyway" which is where things begin to bend

[Verse 2 — Spanish, with English translation]
Dejo mensajes de voz que empiezan con "soy yo"
[I leave voicemails that start with "it's me"]
Como si supiera que me esperas — no lo sé
[As if I knew you were waiting for me — I don't know]
Digo mi nombre dos veces, luego "bueno"
[I say my name twice, then "well"]
Y el mensaje termina sin haber dicho lo que quiero
[And the message ends without having said what I want]

[Chorus — English]
The voicemail knows something I don't know
It knows that what you say and what you mean are quite a show
The voicemail captures everything you thought you'd throw away
The pause before the sentence and the sentence in decay
That's my boy

[Bridge — French, with English translation]
Je laisse des messages vocaux qui commencent par "c'est moi"
[I leave voicemails that start with "it's me"]
Comme si tu savais déjà que c'est moi qui parle là
[As if you already knew it was me speaking there]
La voix enregistrée reste quand la personne part
[The recorded voice stays when the person leaves]
Le message vocal garde quelque chose de son cœur
[The voicemail keeps something of their heart]

[Outro — All three languages]
The voicemail knows… El mensaje de voz sabe… La messagerie vocale sait
The voice outlasts — La voz sobrevive — La voix survit
That's my boy
